rationale: This is a mechanical crossing of two already-tested legs — the frequency accrual leg from RareAccrualYearsSustainedProfit and the turnover-trend conditioner from CashBackedImprovingProductivity (fmb 4.86, t-alpha 3.24) — so it will almost certainly be highly correlated with both parents and teaches little beyond which leg encoding wins, making it a cosmetic recombination rather than a new mechanism.

The short corner is verbatim identical to the short corner of the archived TurnoverFreeTwoSidedQuality and the long corner is just proposal #1, so this is a third-generation reshuffle of the same two-sided template whose incremental information content is essentially nil.

A one-leg encoding swap on the archived AccrualBuildupWeakProfitFloor, but it is internally consistent, asks a genuine and unresolved question (does frequency-based accrual measurement help the short tail or only the long tail), and the answer is diagnostic either way — though the 6-valued count leg will produce coarse, tie-heavy portfolio breakpoints on the short side where dispersion matters most.

This is the one proposal that tests a genuinely new measurement claim — that consistency-of-direction rather than magnitude should encode the *quality* leg as well as the accrual leg — but note the profitability-improvement count is a coarse proxy for the already-used TREND(gp/at,5), so the result will only be interesting if it materially beats that trend-based analogue, and the product of two six-valued counts risks lumpy, unstable decile composition.

The hypothesis-to-expression link is weak and arguably sign-reversed: Δ(dpc/sale) rises mechanically when sales fall or when the firm has just completed a capex cycle, so the leg is far more likely to be picking up revenue deterioration or asset intensity than accounting conservatism, and the archive's own UnderDepreciationMarginGain result (t-alpha −0.22) already suggests this channel carries little independent content.

A defensible single-leg substitution on RareAccrualYearsSustainedProfit that isolates a distinct economic claim (banking cash vs. avoiding accruals), but the cash-build count is likely to load on persistent equity issuers and structurally high-cash industries — partially neutralized by IND_RANK — and the profitability leg is plain Novy-Marx gross profitability, so any positive result needs to be shown incremental to that known anomaly.
